newsitem.title: GERMANY: Karstadt aims for 250 mln DM in savings.
newsitem.headline: Karstadt aims for 250 mln DM in savings.

text.p: German store group Karstadt AG said on Thursday it expected its "Busy" efficiency drive to deliver cost savings of up to 250 million marks by 1999.

Board member Klaus Eierhoff, in charge of the drive to improve data management and relations with suppliers and tighten up on product ranges, said no savings would be achieved this year but savings of 150 million marks would kick in next year.

Moving to more flexible and responsive management methods was vital, Eierhoff said, adding: "We must abandon the inflexible departmental thinking. Otherwise we will increasingly lose contact with our customers."
In addition to the cost savings, Karstadt is looking to modernise its shops along theme-based lines, moving away from the traditional department store model being increasingly shunned by consumers.
Chief executive Walter Deuss said pilot projects in stores in Berlin, Darmstadt and Duisburg had proved positive.
In Duisburg, where a fashion-based store has been opened after a complete renovation, sales growth is running in double digits even though the product line has been narrowed.
Deuss put the price tag on the Duisburg store conversion at around 600 marks per square metre but said costs at other branches could be lower because existing furnishings could be reused.
Executives said no scheme for a comprehensive repackaging of Karstadt outlets had yet been decided on but furthe pilot projects were planned.
Retail sector analysts say that Karstadt is lagging its main competitor, Metro's Kaufhof chain, which has taken a market lead with its successful 'galeria', or mall-type concept.
